summary: Moves the EQL release pipeline (SQL bundle, docs bundle, crate, postgres-eql image, prerelease npm publish) from the dead packages/eql/.github/ directory into the root workflows, gated by a switch derived from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS so it stays inert until the Phase-5 cutover. Two things change today. release.yml, the single npm publishing workflow for all JS and FFI packages, gains workflow_dispatch and a `classify` job that every publish job now depends on. The root rebuild-docs.yml is deleted; per the commit message it never fired. The most material risk is that a dispatch against any branch reads both the arming switch and the release-gate from that branch's own code, so whether the pipeline is inert, and what a prerelease publishes, is decided by unreviewed code. No publish job declares a GitHub `environment:`. Most of the remaining risk sits in the first armed run: npm publishes first and cannot be undone, the other four artefacts follow in separate builds that have never run here, and release-plz publishes the crate on its own trigger without checking the npm release. Static workflow tests cover the gating wiring. None were run and no CI results were available.

behaviour_changes.description: release.yml (npm trusted-publishing workflow for every JS/FFI package) gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger and a `classify` job. `ffi-artifacts`, `publish-ffi` and `release` now also require `needs.classify.outputs.mode == 'production'`, which holds only when GITHUB_REF_NAME is `main`. On a push to main this adds a job but leaves the JS/FFI release unchanged.

A dispatch against a non-main branch whose HEAD subject starts with `chore(release):` is classified `prerelease`. The prerelease jobs create a GitHub release and tags, publish @cipherstash/eql to npm over OIDC, force-create a release/eql-<V> branch and dispatch release-plz.yml. They are gated on the arming switch and the release gate, both computed from the dispatched ref's own checkout.

Adds the production EQL chain to release.yml (eql-sql -> eql-docs -> eql-image dispatch), keyed on @cipherstash/eql appearing in changesets' publishedPackages. Also adds root release-plz.yml (crate publish on push to main under packages/eql/**, or on dispatch) and release-postgres-eql-image.yml (GHCR push, dispatch only). All are gated on `eql-armed`, which is false while @cipherstash/eql is in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS.

Deletes the root rebuild-docs.yml, which POSTed DOCS_WEBHOOK_URL on `@cipherstash/stack@*` tag pushes. According to the commit message, changesets creates those tags with GITHUB_TOKEN, so the workflow never ran. I did not verify that.

EQL npm publish scripts: npm-publish.mjs now sends prereleases to their channel dist-tag (PRE_GA_LATEST=false) rather than `latest`. verify-release-assets.mjs (prepublishOnly) now refuses unless the bundled SQL carries `COMMENT ON SCHEMA eql_v3 IS '<package version>'`; the committed bundle carries '3.0.5', matching package.json.

Lint and test scope expanded: lint-release.yml actionlints the four new workflows and shellchecks the prepare-bindings-assets wrapper, lint-no-workflow-caching.mjs targets the new workflows and audits the docker/release-plz/gpg actions, and the new eql-pipeline-armed.test.mjs pins the exact set of jobs gated on the switch. The packages/eql/.github/ directory is deleted.

failure_scenarios.title: A dispatch against an unmerged branch decides for itself whether EQL publishes and what it publishes
failure_scenarios.trigger: Someone who can dispatch workflows (by mistake, as an insider, or with a compromised token) runs release.yml or release-plz.yml against a branch. The branch's HEAD subject is `chore(release): …`, its package.json pins X.Y.Z-alpha.N, and it deletes the @cipherstash/eql FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry or otherwise edits release-gate.mjs. After the cutover, the deletion is no longer needed.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: `classify` sets mode=prerelease for any non-main ref with that subject (release.yml:84-91). `eql-armed` and `gate` run `node scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs` and `node scripts/release-gate.mjs` from that ref's checkout (release.yml:151, 192), so both answers come from the branch under release. The prerelease jobs then hold contents:write and id-token:write. They create the eql-<V> release and the eql-typescript-v<V> tag, publish the npm package built from the branch, force-update release/eql-<V> and dispatch release-plz.yml there, which reads the switch from that branch again (release-plz.yml:44,73). No publish job declares an `environment:`, so no required reviewer stands between a dispatch and a publish. CODEOWNERS governs merges, not dispatches. Before this change release.yml had no workflow_dispatch.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Before the cutover, npm and crates.io trusted publishing do not name this repository, so the registry publishes should fail. Public eql-<V> GitHub releases with SQL assets, tags and a release branch can still be created in cipherstash/stack from unreviewed code. After the cutover, an @cipherstash/eql prerelease (SQL install bundle embedded) and the eql-bindings crate can be published from an unmerged branch, with valid provenance naming this repository. Publishing cannot be undone, and the SQL is applied to customer databases.

missing_verification: No check that a prerelease publish can only come from a reviewed or protected ref

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Put the publishing jobs (prerelease-eql-*, release, publish-ffi, release-plz `release`, image build) behind a GitHub environment with required reviewers and a deployment-branch policy, or restrict prerelease dispatch to a protected branch pattern. Optionally read the arming switch from the default branch rather than the dispatched ref. Confirm the npm and crates.io trusted-publisher entries pin the environment as well as the workflow filename.

failure_scenarios.title: First armed run publishes npm first, then other artefacts may never follow, or the crate ships alone
failure_scenarios.trigger: The first push to main after the FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry is deleted (Phase-5 cutover), or any later EQL release in which a downstream build fails, or the gate and the switch disagree.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: `release` runs `changeset publish` (irreversible) before eql-sql, eql-docs and eql-image, which then do their own cold builds on Blacksmith runners (release.yml:508-556; _build-eql-sql.yml:80-87). None of these jobs has executed in this repository. Documented prerequisites that no workflow can check in advance (a GPG_PRIVATE_KEY secret and GHCR write access) are missing today (AGENTS.md:358-360). release-plz.yml publishes the crate on its own push trigger, gated only on `eql-armed` and not on the npm release succeeding (release-plz.yml:26-44, 75-78). The production npm publish is held by `gate`, not by `eql-armed`, and AGENTS.md:343-355 states nothing asserts the two agree.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Version V of @cipherstash/eql reaches npm with no matching eql-V SQL release, docs bundle or postgres-eql image. Or eql-bindings V reaches crates.io while the npm release was blocked. The single-version promise across five artefacts breaks, nothing reports it as a release failure, and recovery means hand-dispatching or cutting a new version.

failure_scenarios.title: SQL on the GitHub release and in the image is rebuilt from source rather than taken from the npm tarball
failure_scenarios.trigger: An armed production or prerelease EQL release, built with a different `rust latest` toolchain or environment than the one that ran `pnpm run version`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The npm package ships the SQL committed by the version hook and checked by verify-release-assets.mjs. _build-eql-sql.yml instead regenerates SQL with `mise run --force build --version` at publish time (lines 80-87), and the image workflow builds it a third time. The version stamp will match in every case. AGENTS.md:427-431 records that nothing proves regeneration reproduces the published bytes.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The eql-V GitHub release asset or the image can carry SQL bytes that differ from npm's under the same version and stamp. A digest comparison against the npm release manifest fails, or a different function body is installed depending on which channel a customer used.

existing_verification.description: eql-sql-asset-freshness.test.mjs compares the version and stamp across the in-tree artefacts, not the bytes rebuilt in CI.

missing_verification: No digest comparison between the rebuilt SQL and the committed or npm-bundled release-manifest before attaching
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Attach the committed packages/eql/packages/eql/sql bundle (or verify the rebuilt file's digest against its release-manifest.json) instead of shipping a fresh build.

The armed pipeline has never run end to end in this repository. Its first execution is the cutover release.
None of the changed script tests were run: no CI results were provided and node_modules is absent, so vitest could not run.

recommended_controls.description: Review release.yml's `classify` and prerelease jobs, and release-plz.yml's dispatch trigger, for who can start a credentialed publish and from which refs.
Add a protected GitHub environment (required reviewers, deployment-branch policy) to every publishing job, and bind the npm and crates.io trusted publishers to it.
Add a test asserting `release-gate.mjs` and `eql-pipeline-armed.mjs` agree on @cipherstash/eql, and that release-plz's publish depends on the npm version being on the registry.

Before deleting the FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry, provision GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and GHCR access, rehearse with a prerelease identity, and write down how to hand-dispatch the SQL, docs and image jobs if they fail after npm has published.
Verify the rebuilt SQL digest against the committed release-manifest.json before attaching it to the GitHub release or baking it into the image.
Run `pnpm test:scripts` (or confirm CI ran it green) on head before merge.

evidence.claim: release.yml gains a `workflow_dispatch: {}` trigger, which it did not have at base.
classify: mode=production only when GITHUB_REF_NAME is main; any other ref whose HEAD subject is `chore(release):*` becomes prerelease, after a version-shape check and an existing-tag short-circuit.
eql-armed and gate both check out the triggering ref and run scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs and scripts/release-gate.mjs from it.
The switch is `!FROZEN_PUBLISHERS.has('@cipherstash/eql')`, imported from the checked-out release-gate.mjs.
prerelease-eql-npm holds id-token:write and contents:write, builds from the dispatched sha, runs npm-publish.mjs and creates the eql-typescript-v<V> tag.
prerelease-eql-crate creates or force-updates release/eql-<V> at the run's sha and dispatches release-plz.yml on it.
No job in the three publishing workflows declares a GitHub environment (no output).
release-plz.yml is dispatchable, reads the switch from the triggering ref, and its release job holds id-token:write and contents:write.
@cipherstash/eql is frozen because npm provenance names encrypt-query-language and release.yml carries no NPM_TOKEN, so a registry publish from here should currently fail.
Tests the switch in both states and pins the exact list of jobs whose `if:` text contains the eql-armed condition. Nothing about refs or environments.
The JS `release` job now needs classify and requires mode == 'production' in addition to gate success.
The EQL version is resolved from changesets' publishedPackages after the npm publish, and eql-sql then builds and creates the eql-<V> release.
The SQL release assets are regenerated with `mise run --force build --version` in CI and attached to a new release, not copied from the committed bundle.
mise pins rust `latest` and nothing proves regenerating the SQL reproduces npm's published bytes.
The crate publish runs on push to main under packages/eql/** and is gated only on eql-armed, with no dependency on release.yml's npm publish.
The cutover still needs a GPG_PRIVATE_KEY secret and GHCR write access, and no workflow can assert either in advance.
The deleted root workflow POSTed DOCS_WEBHOOK_URL on `@cipherstash/stack@*` tag pushes. The commit message says it never ran because those tags are created with GITHUB_TOKEN.
PRE_GA_LATEST flipped to false, so prereleases publish under alpha/beta/rc rather than latest.
prepublishOnly now requires the exact version stamp in the SQL bundle. The committed bundle carries '3.0.5', matching package.json 3.0.5.
release-postgres-eql-image.yml historically co-changed with release-eql.yml, which does not exist at head. The pipeline shape changed rather than the file being forgotten.
No node_modules in the checkout, so the vitest script tests could not be run offline.
The image workflow is dispatch-only, gated on eql-armed, and rebuilds SQL itself from the dispatched ref with a free-form eql_version input.
The production npm publish is held by `gate`, not by `eql-armed`, and nothing asserts the two agree.
